notes: A, B, C, D, H and O are solved directly in the canonical robot frame; no display-time mirror or solver-to-robot rotation is part of the physical model.
The directed vector D->A has angle -30 degrees from +Ox, so A->D has angle +150 degrees and D is higher than A.
The pose variable ab_angle is the directed angle of A->B measured directly from robot +Ox; it is a geometric coordinate, not yet a calibrated motor encoder angle.
The physical four-bar topology places B on the right side of directed A->D and C on the right side of directed B->D.
B, C and O are fixed material points of one rigid wheel-carrier body.
H and O are derived from the moving B->C basis: e_BC=(C-B)/BC, H=B-BH*e_BC, and O=H+OH*n_BC on the configured side of B->C.
H is an auxiliary construction point, not a joint or degree of freedom.
